Render a change table to HTML or PDF

Source: R/yoy_render.R
yoyren.Rd

Writes a change table from yoy() to a file for people who will not run R: yoyhtml() to a single self-contained web page, yoypdf() to a PDF. Each row shows the period, the value, the previous value, the change and the percent change, coloured by whether it is better or worse, with the exact interval and any flags; the HTML page also has summary cards from yoysmry(). Use them to hand a reviewed set of period-over-period changes to a manager, a journalist or a court.

Usage

yoyhtml(
  x,
  file,
  title = "Year-over-year change",
  sub = NULL,
  pal = "diverging",
  digits = 1L,
  bars = TRUE,
  intv = TRUE,
  notes = NULL,
  ...
)

yoypdf(
  x,
  file,
  title = "Year-over-year change",
  sub = NULL,
  pal = "diverging",
  digits = 1L,
  intv = TRUE,
  notes = NULL,
  width = 11,
  height = 8.5,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

An rmbl_yoy object from yoy(), written as HTML.

file

Output path (a string). yoyhtml() writes a single self-contained HTML file with no external requests; yoypdf() writes a PDF using R's own device, so neither needs a package beyond base R.

title

Heading for the page (and the HTML page title or PDF title), a string; default "Year-over-year change".

sub

Optional line under the heading. Defaults to the table's own settings – lag, units, interval and base gate – so the reader can see what the percentages mean.

pal

One of yoypals(): "diverging" (the default), "safe" or "mono".

digits

Digits for the percent column, default 1.

bars

Logical (HTML only): draw an in-cell bar proportional to the change, scaled to the largest absolute change in the table (default TRUE).

intv

Logical: show the exact interval column for counts (default TRUE).

notes

Optional character vector of footnotes.

...

Further arguments; the HTML writer does not use them.

width, height

PDF page size in inches (default 11 by 8.5, landscape US letter).

Value

The path file, invisibly.

Details

Neither backend needs a package beyond base R. The HTML page inlines its stylesheet, makes no external requests (no fonts, scripts or images from the network) and escapes every value, so the file stays the artefact and renders the same later. Rows are coloured by the table's verdict: "worse" in the palette's bad colour, "better" in its good colour, everything else (including the "up" and "down" of direction = "neutral") in its neutral grey. Labels set with yoylbl() replace the period. For percentage units the change is shown in points. The page ends with the package version that wrote it.

The PDF is drawn on R's own pdf() device with its standard fonts, which cannot draw arrows or dashes, so those are written in ASCII (+, -). Long tables are split over pages at 0.22 inch per row, with “page i of n” labels; notes go under the last page's rows when they fit and on pages of their own otherwise. The interval column appears only when the table has pctlo and pctup (counts).

Both overwrite file. Errors: x not from yoy(); a pal not in yoypals(); a file that cannot be written.

Examples

d <- data.frame(year = rep(2019:2023, each = 2),
                region = rep(c("North", "South"), 5),
                n = c(31, 402, 28, 377, 12, 190, 19, 268, 24, 331))
y <- yoy(d, value = "n", prd = "year", by = "region",
         dir = "lower")

h <- file.path(tempdir(), "change.html")
yoyhtml(y, h, title = "Placements by region")
file.exists(h)
#> [1] TRUE

p <- file.path(tempdir(), "change.pdf")
yoypdf(y, p, title = "Placements by region")
file.exists(p)
#> [1] TRUE

# a colour-blind-safe palette, no bars or intervals, and a footnote
yoyhtml(y, h, pal = "safe", bars = FALSE, intv = FALSE,
         notes = "Counts below 10 are suppressed at source.")
any(grepl("suppressed", readLines(h)))
#> [1] TRUE

# portrait letter pages, with fiscal-year labels
yoypdf(yoylbl(y, fylbl), p, width = 8.5, height = 11)

# only yoy() tables can be rendered
try(yoyhtml(d, h))
#> Error : yoyhtml: `x` must be an rmbl_yoy object from yoy()
unlink(c(h, p))
